ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are five circles sandwiched between the same pair of non-parallel straight lines, the upper straight line is labeled L1, and the lower straight line is labeled L2. The five circles are tangent in sequence from left to right, and all are simultaneously tangent to L1 and L2; the sizes of the circles gradually increase from left to right, so the middle circle is the third circle. Reasoning: Extend L1 and L2 so that they intersect at a vertex, and let half of the angle between the two straight lines be alpha. Each circle is tangent to the two straight lines, so the centers of the circles all lie on the same angle bisector. If the radius of a certain circle is r, then the distance from its center to the vertex is r/sin(alpha). For two adjacent tangent circles, suppose their radii are respectively r and R, then the distance between their centers on the angle bisector is (R-r)/sin(alpha). On the other hand, the two circles are externally tangent, so the distance between the centers is also equal to r+R. Therefore (R-r)/sin(alpha)=r+R, which derives that R/r is a constant determined only by alpha. Thus the radii of the five circles form a geometric sequence. The radius of the smallest circle is 8, the radius of the largest circle is 18, and the five radii are r1,r2,r3,r4,r5, where r1=8 and r5=18. In a geometric sequence, the third term is the geometric mean of the first term and the fifth term, so r3=sqrt(8*18)=sqrt(144)=12.

From the image, identify that the five circles lie between the same two nonparallel tangent lines L1 and L2, increase from left to right, and are tangent consecutively; the middle circle is the third one. From the text, take the smallest radius as 8 and the largest radius as 18. Extend L1 and L2 to meet at a vertex, and let the half-angle between the lines be alpha. Since each circle is tangent to both lines, each center lies on the same angle bisector and a circle of radius r has center distance r/sin(alpha) from the vertex. For two consecutive tangent circles of radii r and R, the distance between their centers along the angle bisector is (R-r)/sin(alpha), but external tangency also makes it r+R. Thus (R-r)/sin(alpha)=r+R, so R/r is a constant depending only on the angle. Therefore the five radii form a geometric progression. With r1=8 and r5=18, r3 is the geometric mean of r1 and r5: r3=sqrt(8*18)=12.
